title: BNN-YEO: an efficient Bayesian Neural Network for yield estimation and optimization
problem: Yield estimation and optimization in large-scale circuits is computationally expensive due to high transistor-level simulation costs and limited computational resources, making it impractical for modern chip designs.
motivation: Yield estimation and optimization are critical for circuit design success, but remain prohibitively expensive for large-scale chips due to simulation overhead.
method: The approach uses a Bayesian Neural Network—a neural network that represents uncertainty through probability—to build a surrogate model (a simplified stand-in for expensive chip simulations). It integrates prior knowledge (information we already have) with new data to avoid overfitting, where the model would just memorize training cases rather than learn general patterns. To optimize yield (the percentage of working chips), the method replaces the sharp on/off behavior of yield thresholds with a smooth mathematical approximation, enabling gradient-based optimization (using calculus to find the best design changes). This avoids expensive Monte Carlo simulation (random sampling to estimate outcomes).
key_novelty: The key innovation is enabling gradient-based yield optimization (using calculus to improve designs) by smoothing sharp yield decision boundaries into continuous curves, while using a Bayesian Neural Network that integrates prior knowledge to prevent overfitting.
contributions: Novel BNN-YEO framework achieving 100x speedup over Monte Carlo for yield estimation
Bayesian approach that effectively integrates prior knowledge and prevents overfitting in surrogate models
Smooth indicator function approximation enabling gradient-based global optimization
20x speedup over state-of-the-art with improved accuracy for combined yield estimation and optimization
baselines: state-of-the-art yield estimation and optimization methods
primary_theme: machine learning based circuit yield optimization
